title: The residue-field fibre module is the localization of the prime quotient
statement: Let $\varphi:A\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, let $\mathfrak p\subset A$ be prime, and let $N$ be a $B$-module. Put $U=\varphi(A\setminus\mathfrak p)$ and $M=N/\mathfrak pN$, where $\mathfrak pN$ is the $B$-submodule generated by $\varphi(a)n$ for $a\in\mathfrak p$, $n\in N$. There is a canonical $B$-linear isomorphism $N\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p)\cong U^{-1}M$ sending $n\otimes\overline{a/s}$ to $\overline{\varphi(a)n}/\varphi(s)$; its inverse sends $\bar n/\varphi(s)$ to $n\otimes\overline{1/s}$. Here $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is the residue field [def-weil-residue-field], tensor is [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], and localization is [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. Moreover, if $\mathfrak q\subset B$ is prime with $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)=\mathfrak p$ and $z\in M$ has $\operatorname{Ann}_B(z)=\mathfrak q$, then $\operatorname{Ann}_B(z/1)=\mathfrak q$ in $U^{-1}M$, and hence the image of $z/1$ in the fibre has the same annihilator [def-weil-pbc-annihilator-associated-primes].
